full_judgment:
14. With regard to the interpolation of the date stamped on the application form, even if the petitioner admits that the application was filed on 11-8-1991, the acceptance by the Office of the Registrar that the application was filed on 11-8-1991 without further inquiry as to who has overwritten the date on the application form, is not satisfactory. If the interpolation has taken place in the Office of the Registrar it is his duty to examine who has caused such interpolation before accepting the explanation of the applicant or the noting of his officer to the effect that is was a mistake, It is highly inconceivable that in the month of August a date stamp for the following year would have been mistakenly put upon the application form. Such a mistake in the date stamp may be acceptable if it had occurred in the month of December or January with the change of the year, but cannot be acceptable when the mistake apparently occurred in month of August. How the date 11 AUG 1992 could have been stamped on 11 AUG 1991 is beyond comprehension. The Office of the Registrar was wrong to accept the explanation without examining the matter. Moreover, it is curious that the mistake was not noticed either by the officers in the Registrar's office when the registration certificate was first issued on 20-3-2001 or by the applicant when he received the same nor when the renewal was sent on 6-12-2001. Clearly the opposite party No. 1 was aroused after Rule was issued in the matter on 27-10-2002, which was communicated by special messenger and received on 5-11-2002 by Sanowara Corporation on behalf of opposite party No.1. On 10-11-2002 the applicant brought the matter to the notice of the Registrar, more than 10 years after the application had been lodged. 

 20. Nevertheless, in spite of the claim of Sanowara that Bonlac has acquiesced to the applicant's use of the trademark and its claim that the petitioner is not a person aggrieved, I am inclined to hold the view that this Court has power under section 46(4) to act where the application has been filed on a misrepresentation of fact; where there is apparent interpolation of the records; where there has been illegal restoration of the abandoned application. Under the aforementioned provision of law, I hold that the Register of Trade Marks is liable to be rectified by expunging the registration of application No.33243 filed by Unilac Sanowara (BD) Limited. I am satisfied that both the contesting parties have had notice regarding the matters discussed above, sufficient opportunity was given to the parties to address the issues arising and I have heard their arguments at length.
